checkpoints.question: How is a store locator laid out for a body?
Which error is raised when a locator escapes the warmpool root?

forbidden_claims: that the locator's directory name proves containment
that escaping locators are impossible because ids are hashed

items.body:
def test_store_refuses_a_tampered_body(warmpool, store):
    from ptr_engine.errors import PtrHashMismatchError

    ref = store.put(b"trust me")
    store.path_of(ref).write_bytes(b"trust me!")
    with pytest.raises(PtrHashMismatchError) as excinfo:
        store.get(ref)
    assert excinfo.value.code == "PTR_HASH_MISMATCH"

long_run.what_grows: 72 turns of adversarial cases; the escape list grows and each new attempt is judged against the hashing contract fixed at turn 3, so early context must survive the whole run.

objective: Make BodyStore.path_of refuse any locator that escapes the warmpool root without weakening content addressing.

repair.correct_action: The locator is caller-supplied on the ResourceRef; keep the resolved-path containment check and treat any non-hash-prefixed locator as a store miss. Restore the check removed at turn 14.
repair.wrong_assumption: The locator is safe to join because its first path component is a hash prefix.
